subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Grounding: The Safety Path
description: One-minute skill: Grounding: The Safety Path.

hook.text: Touch a faulty appliance and current can flow through your body. Grounding stops that.

buildup.text: A ground wire connects metal cases to the earth via a buried rod or pipe.

discovery.text: If a wire touches the case, current takes the easy ground path — not through you.

twist.text: The earth is a huge conductor. It absorbs stray current without voltage rise.

climax.text: A breaker trips when ground current spikes, cutting power in milliseconds.

punchline.text: The ground wire is the escape route current takes instead of you.

quiz.question: What does a ground wire do in a faulty appliance?
options: It increases the voltage to blow the fuse faster
It gives stray current an easy path to earth instead of through a person
It stores excess charge in the metal casing
